content: Lanolin is a non-petroleum-based lubricant that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of diaper dermatitis and for protecting chafed skin or minor skin irritations caused by incontinence. Common adverse reactions include burning, stinging, redness, and irritation. Pediatric Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications and Dosage (Pediatric): Lanolin helps prevent and treat diaper dermatitis. It protects chafed skin or minor skin irritations caused by incontinence and helps seal out wetness. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Pediatric): Guideline-Supported Use: There is limited information available regarding off-label guideline-supported use of lanolin in pediatric patients. Contraindications There is limited information available regarding contraindications for lanolin in the drug label. Warnings For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes. Do not apply to deep or puncture wounds. If the condition worsens or does not improve within 7 days, consult a doctor. Keep out of reach of children. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately.
